    Age 5 — Dwarf Era

    The Romanium Economy¶

    The foundation of this prosperity was Romanium — a perfect metal, almost indestructible, that held an edge forever. A sword made of Romanium would never dull, never rust, never break. Armor forged from it was impenetrable. Tools crafted from it lasted for generations.

    Dwarven mines produced Romanium in abundance, and dwarven forges turned it into the finest manufactured goods on Ge'or:

    • Weapons — swords, axes, spears of legendary quality.
    • Tools — hammers, chisels, plows that never wore out.
    • Magical items and staffs — the most efficient ever created, their enchantments preserved in Romanium's perfect crystalline structure.
    • Commodities — everyday goods of a quality no other species could match.

    During the Dwarf Era, gold, food, and silver were as cheap as water. Everyone — human, elf, demon — had access to high-quality manufactured goods. The standard of living across the known world was higher than at any point since the Glorious Alliance.

    The Slow Decline¶

    Prosperity is fragile. Romanium was the foundation, and Romanium was finite.

    As ore reserves began to dwindle, the economy entered a slow, grinding decline. It was not a sudden catastrophe. It was a generation-by-generation erosion — mines producing less each year, prices rising, trade routes shrinking. Dwarven cities that had bustled with commerce grew quiet. Forges that had burned for centuries went cold.

    The dwarves tried to adapt — deeper mines, more efficient extraction, recycling old Romanium. None of it was enough. The ore was running out, and with it, the foundation of their civilization.

    The Golden War¶

    As dwarven power weakened, others saw opportunity. Human nomads from West and North Erisdar — mounted on horses (descendants of animals carried aboard the Glorious Alliance) — began raiding dwarven territories.

    What started as raids became a war. The Golden War — named for the wealth the nomads sought — swept across the declining dwarven realms. Dwarven outposts were overrun. Trade caravans were ambushed. The megacities, once impenetrable, became islands in a sea of raiders.

    The dwarves survived. But their age was over.

    Legacy — The Legendary Relics¶

    Items from the Dwarf Era are considered legendary relics in the present day. They command insane prices on the black market and in the collections of emperors and merchant princes. A verified Dwarf Era blade is worth more than a kingdom's annual tax revenue.

    The qualities that made them legendary:

    • Romanium swords — indestructible. They will never lose their edge, never rust, never break. A Dwarf Era blade found in a tomb after five thousand years will be as sharp as the day it was forged.
    • Romanium armor — impenetrable by conventional weapons. Surviving sets are priceless.
    • Magical items and staffs — the most efficient ever created. Modern mages who wield Dwarf Era artifacts are universally recognized as the most powerful practitioners alive. The Romanium's crystalline structure somehow preserves and amplifies enchantments in ways that modern craftsmen cannot replicate.

    The Dwarves of the present day remember this age with pride and sorrow. They once built a world. They lost it to geology and raiders.

    Connections¶

    [ Age 5 — The Dwarf Era ] ├── Span: ~5,499 to 4,500 BGD ├── Preceded By: Age 4 — Dragon Tyranny ├── Succeeded By: Age 6 — Iron Age ├── Dominant Species: Dwarves — megacities, global trade ├── Foundation: Romanium — perfect metal, now nearly extinct ├── Golden War: Human horse-nomad raiders from West/North Erisdar ├── Legacy: Legendary relics — indestructible weapons, perfect magical items ├── Centers: Dwarvengor + underground megacities worldwide ├── Economy: Unprecedented prosperity — gold, food, silver as cheap as water └── Cause of Decline: Romanium depletion — slow, generational, irreversible

    50–100 Year Transition¶

    With Romanium gone, the dwarves retreated deeper into their mountains. The surface species were forced to fall back on iron — an inferior metal, abundant but crude. It was a technological downgrade, a civilizational shame. The Age 6 — Iron Age was not an advancement. It was the best anyone could do with what was left.
